Protein Food

T-Bone Steak

About This Entry

T-bone combines strip steak and tenderloin separated by a T-shaped bone, offering two textures in one cut. The strip side brings marbling and beef intensity; the tenderloin side stays lean and mild — versatile for structured reds.

Beginner Guide

A T-bone is two steaks in one: striploin on one side of the bone, tenderloin on the other. Porterhouse uses the same idea but from a larger section with a bigger tenderloin portion.

FAQ

What is T-Bone Steak?
A T-bone is two steaks in one: striploin on one side of the bone, tenderloin on the other.
How should T-Bone Steak be cooked for best results?
Rich cuts tolerate medium to medium-rare; render fat slowly on roasts and braises. Rest before serving so juices redistribute.
